subject: Dedicated commit, burst & overage policy - CloudWave negotiation
messages:
From: Sarah Patel <sarah@cloudwave.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@cloudwave.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial questions on Dedicated commit & burst behavior

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the throughput looked great. Before we take this to procurement, two quick questions from our infra/ops team: 

1) When we commit a pool (e.g., 8 A100-equivalent GPUs), can CloudWave burst above that commit for short windows? If so, what pricing/limits apply?
2) How do you meter "above-commit" usage? Is it per-GPU-hour, per-token, or per-request basis?

We’d also like to understand soft vs. hard throttling behavior: do you queue requests when capacity is constrained, degrade to smaller model, or return a 429?

If you can send a short bullet summary, we’ll route to finance/procurement.

—Sarah
Senior Platform Engineer, CloudWave

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah@cloudwave.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial questions on Dedicated commit & burst behavior

Hi Sarah — great to chat. TL;DR below, then more detail.

- Burst: yes, short bursts allowed by policy; billed as above-commit at a tiered rate and subject to pool-level smoothing.
- Metering: above-commit metered per-GPU-minute (rounded to nearest minute) for dedicated pools; model variant surcharges may apply.
- Throttling: platform prefers soft degradation (auto-fallback to compatible smaller variant or reduced max batch size) before returning 429s; customers can opt into stricter enforcement.

Details: 
1) Burst windows: default burst is 20% above committed capacity sustained for up to 10 minutes on average over a 1-hour rolling window. Admins can set custom burst policy in the Dedicated config; sustained excess triggers either spillover to burst-backed on-demand capacity (if enabled) or metered overage.

2) Billing: Overage is metered and invoiced monthly. Primary unit is GPU-minute at the provisioned SKU with multipliers for model complexity (e.g., 1.0x for baseline, 1.3x for large context/FP16 workloads). We provide a post-aggregation CSV of minute-level usage for reconciliation.

3) Soft vs hard enforcement: Default behavior: 1) prefix/KV cache attempts to absorb bursts, 2) auto-batch tuning reduces per-request memory, 3) fallback to pinned smaller model variant (if configured), then 4) 429 with retry-after header. Customers can request a hard throttle policy (stop at commit) or an aggressive overage cap to limit invoiced spend.

Attaching a short draft of the committed usage plan and the SLA routing spec (see attachments).

Next steps: if you want a capped overage or a negotiated blended rate for above-commit, loop in procurement and Marcus (copied) and we’ll prepare pricing options.

—Neha
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah@cloudwave.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, procure@cloudwave.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial questions on Dedicated commit & burst behavior

Thanks both — adding a few commercial points for procurement: 

1) Discount tiers: our standard reserved-commit discounts kick in at 3-month minimum commitments: 1–4 GPUs (base discount 10%), 5–16 GPUs (18%), 17+ GPUs (28%). We can offer a one-time early-commit carveout for CloudWave given expected volume.

2) Overage pricing: standard is 1.8x the committed unit rate for on-demand GPU-minute billing. For customers who purchase >=12-month reserved commits we can reduce overage multiplier to 1.25x.

3) Overage cap option: we can include an optional monthly cap (e.g., 20% of committed spend) beyond which we will hard-throttle. If CloudWave prefers, we will notify and request authorization to continue charging.

4) Metering & reconciliation: we send detailed usage CSVs and provide a 30-day window for dispute before final invoice. Billing team will expose APIs for real-time spend telemetry.

If these look reasonable we’ll draft a pricing appendix and SOW. Laura — want to approve the early-commit carveout draft?

—Marcus
Head of Commercials, Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Patel <sarah@cloudwave.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@cloudwave.com, market_ops@cloudwave.com (Billing)
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 12:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial questions on Dedicated commit & burst behavior

Appreciate the clarity. A few follow-ups from procurement/billing: 

- The 1.8x overage multiplier on GPU-minute seems steep; procurement would prefer a blended incremental rate per GPU-minute that is a fixed delta (e.g., +$0.65/GPU-minute) for the first 30% overage and then higher beyond that.
- Can you provide sample invoices / a pro-forma showing committed vs. burst billing for a representative month (8-GPU commit with 12 hours of 30% burst)?
- Confirmation that we can enable the monthly cap and opt into hard-throttle if we hit it. If so, we’ll include that as a contractual SLA clause.

Also, we need the metering CSV format and timezones for usage timestamps — can you ensure everything is in UTC?

—Sarah

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah@cloudwave.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, procure@cloudwave.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial questions on Dedicated commit & burst behavior

Hi Sarah — jumping in from solutions/ops: we mocked a pro-forma for an 8-GPU commit with the usage profile you requested and attached the CSV and a small model of charges (attached as Committed_Usage_Plan.pdf). Key notes: 

- In our example, 30% sustained burst for 12 hours (spread across the month) added ~15% incremental spend compared to commit-only billing under the 1.8x rule. Using a blended delta (+$0.65/GPU-minute for first 30%) reduces that incremental spend to ~7% in the example.
- Metering export is UTC, minute-granular with fields: timestamp_utc, pool_id, sku, gpu_minutes, multiplier, billed_amount_usd. We’ll include a sample export in the Drive link.
- For the monthly cap: we can add a clause that triggers hard-throttle at a configurable percentage of committed spend; notifications and an approval flow will be sent.

If helpful, we can run your org’s last 30 days through our simulator to produce a tailored estimate.

—Priyom
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Patel <sarah@cloudwave.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, procure@cloudwave.com, market_ops@cloudwave.com (Billing)
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial questions on Dedicated commit & burst behavior

Thanks — that is exactly what procurement wanted. Two quick items before we escalate to legal: 

1) Please include the blended delta option (+$0.65/GPU-minute up to first 30% overage) in the pricing appendix, and an explicit monthly cap term (20% of committed spend by default, adjustable).
2) For invoicing disputes we need a 45-day dispute window (you currently have 30). Can Redwood accommodate 45 days?

If you can confirm those two points in writing and send a short pricing appendix draft, we’ll move to an LOA and then legal review.

—Sarah

On a separate note: appreciate the UTC metering export — that will help our billing team reconcile automatically.
